study_identification_part.si_4_title: Using normative modeling and machine learning for detecting mild traumatic brain injury from magnetoencephalography data

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: Cam-CAN is the Cambridge Centre for Ageing and Neuroscience dataset, a large open neuroimaging dataset containing MEG and MRI measurements of nearly 700 healthy participants aged 18 to 87. The SINGLE-SITE dataset comprises MEG recordings from 25 mTBI patients and 20 healthy controls originally measured by Kaltiainen and colleagues at Aalto Neuroimaging MEG Core, Aalto University School of Science, Espoo, Finland.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "We employed a dataset originally measured by Kaltiainen and colleagues [27,28], comprising resting-state MEG recordings from 25 mild traumatic injury patients and 20 healthy controls. In addition, we employed a large, separate dataset, utilizing MEG recordings from a total of 621 healthy participants [29] as normative data." ... "A large open neuroimaging dataset by the Cambridge Centre for Ageing and Neuroscience (Cam-CAN) [29], containing MEG and MRI measurements of nearly 700 healthy participants aged 18 to 87, was used for creating the normative reference data."

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: The Cam-CAN dataset was used to determine the variation in power spectra across the cortex and to calculate normative Z-scores. The mean and standard deviation of power spectra were calculated across the Cam-CAN subjects to obtain normative models. Three types of normative models were constructed: full (all ages), age-matched subsets, and random subsets. The SINGLE-SITE patient/control dataset was used to train and validate SVM classifiers to discriminate mTBI patients from healthy controls using deviation maps computed from the normative models.

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: The study constructed normative models using 621 subjects from Cam-CAN. The full normative model used all 621 subjects. Age-matched normative models were also created using subsets of subjects within the same age decade as the patient/control being evaluated. The number of subjects per age group was: 56 (18-27), 92 (28-37), 104 (38-47), 93 (48-57), 95 (58-67), 102 (68-77), 79 (78-87). No explicit train/test split was reported for the normative model construction itself; the entire normative dataset was used to compute mean and standard deviation statistics.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: "Subjects with missing or incomplete resting-state MEG measurements or T1-weighted MRI images were excluded from the analyses, resulting in a set of 621 subjects. The number of subjects in each age group was 56, 92, 104, 93, 95, 102 and 79, from the youngest to oldest."

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: The Cam-CAN dataset contains participants aged 18 to 87 years, with approximately 50 men and 50 women in each age decade (18-27, 28-37, 38-47, 48-57, 58-67, 68-77, 78-87 years). The paper reports only the age range (min=18, max=87) for the normative dataset. Mean, SD, median, and IQR were not reported. Given the curated cross-sectional design with roughly equal distribution across decades, a rough estimate of mean age would be approximately in the mid-50s, but this was not explicitly stated.
dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.supporting_text: "A large open neuroimaging dataset by the Cambridge Centre for Ageing and Neuroscience (Cam-CAN) [29], containing MEG and MRI measurements of nearly 700 healthy participants aged 18 to 87, was used for creating the normative reference data. The curated, cross-sectional Cam-CAN dataset contains measurements from approximately 50 men and 50 women in each age decade (18-27, 28-37, 38-47, 48-57, 58-67, 68-77 and 78-87 years)."

dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: The paper states that the Cam-CAN dataset contains approximately 50 men and 50 women in each age decade. With 621 subjects total across 7 age decades, the approximate sex distribution can be inferred as roughly 50% female and 50% male (approximately 310-311 each). Exact counts were not reported in this paper.
